The approach library

Go deeper into the work.

Each guide explains an approach, walks through a fictional example, and explores sessions, limitations, and questions. Educational inclusion does not mean every approach is currently offered by M.F.T.

Cognitive Behavioral TherapyCBT connects what happens, how you interpret it, how you feel, and what you do next. Learn the model, see a worked example, and understand what the work can involve.Explore this approach →Acceptance and Commitment TherapyACT connects acceptance, perspective, values, and action. Explore how psychological flexibility differs from giving up, controlling every thought, or waiting to feel ready before living.Explore this approach →Attachment-based therapyAttachment-based therapy explores how relationship experiences shape expectations and responses. Learn what the perspective can illuminate without treating attachment labels as fixed identities.Explore this approach →Behavioral activationBehavioral activation explores the relationship between mood, activity, avoidance, and reinforcement. Learn how a carefully sized plan differs from keeping busy or being told to try harder.Explore this approach →Bowen family systems therapyBowen theory considers the family as an emotional system. Explore differentiation, triangles, and family patterns without treating them as diagnoses or instructions to reconnect with unsafe people.Explore this approach →Child-centered play therapyExplore a relationship-based play-therapy model, the purpose of child-led choice, the role of limits, and how caregiver collaboration can support the work.Explore this approach →Dialectical Behavior Therapy skillsDBT brings acceptance and change together. Explore how its skills work, what a session can involve, and why learning DBT skills is not the same as enrolling in a full DBT program.Explore this approach →Discernment counselingLearn how discernment counseling differs from couples therapy when partners are uncertain about staying together, what its paths mean, and why it does not promise reconciliation.Explore this approach →Emotion regulation skillsUnderstand emotion regulation as noticing, interpreting, and responding to emotions, not suppressing them. Explore the difference between coping in a moment and changing longer patterns.Explore this approach →Emotionally Focused TherapyEmotionally Focused Therapy explores emotion and attachment in relationships. Learn how a therapist may work with a repeating interaction, why vulnerability needs safety, and what EFT does not promise.Explore this approach →Existential therapyExistential therapy explores meaning, choice, uncertainty, connection, and the limits of life. Learn how philosophical questions can become practical without turning difficult circumstances into a failure to choose well.Explore this approach →Experiential therapyExperiential therapies use present-moment emotional or relational experience as part of the work. Learn what an invitation might involve and why consent, meaning, and integration matter more than intensity.Explore this approach →Exposure-based therapyExposure-based treatments involve planned contact with feared but appropriately safe situations or experiences. Learn the rationale, the importance of consent, and why the exact protocol and assessment matter.Explore this approach →Family systems therapyFamily systems therapy considers relationships, roles, and context. Explore how a systemic perspective differs from blaming a family, requiring everyone to attend, or treating all responsibility as equal.Explore this approach →Gottman-informed couples therapyExplore the relationship foundations, conflict practices, and shared meaning emphasized in Gottman-informed work, with examples that distinguish a useful repair from pressure to move on.Explore this approach →Grief-focused therapyExplore how grief-focused support can address loss, daily life, meaning, and connection without imposing a timetable or treating every grief experience as a disorder.Explore this approach →Integrative therapyLearn what it means to combine therapy approaches thoughtfully, how a coherent plan differs from a collection of techniques, and what questions help you understand the work.Explore this approach →Internal Family Systems-informed therapyIFS uses the language of parts to explore competing feelings and protective responses. Learn what that model means, how a session may feel, and why consent and pacing remain essential.Explore this approach →Mindfulness-based therapyMindfulness-based approaches work with attention and awareness. Learn how a practice can be used in therapy, why it is not thought suppression, and how discomfort or accessibility needs should shape the plan.Explore this approach →Motivational interviewingMotivational interviewing helps explore mixed feelings about change. Learn how collaboration, careful listening, and your own reasons differ from persuasion, pressure, or a therapist choosing for you.Explore this approach →Narrative therapyNarrative therapy explores identity, meaning, and the influence of problems. Learn how separating a person from a problem can make room for agency without denying facts or responsibility.Explore this approach →Parent coachingUnderstand caregiver-focused support, the difference between coaching and child treatment, and how specific routines and responses can be reviewed without blaming a parent or child.Explore this approach →Person-centered therapyPerson-centered therapy emphasizes an empathic, genuine, accepting relationship. Learn what client-led work can involve, how it differs from passive listening, and how to discuss the amount of structure you need.Explore this approach →Play therapyUnderstand the difference between therapeutic play and ordinary recreation, how caregivers may be involved, and why training and development matter when choosing play therapy.Explore this approach →Psychodynamic therapyPsychodynamic therapy explores recurring emotional and relationship patterns, including meanings that are not immediately obvious. Learn how insight can connect with present choices and a collaborative therapeutic relationship.Explore this approach →Sex therapyUnderstand what sex therapy addresses, how it differs from medical treatment, and what respectful boundaries, consent, and collaborative goals should look like.Explore this approach →Solution-Focused Brief TherapySolution-focused therapy explores a preferred future, useful exceptions, and small signs of change. See how its questions differ from forced optimism or advice to simply try harder.Explore this approach →Solution-focused couples therapyExplore a solution-focused style of couples work: preferred changes, exceptions to a repeating problem, and small next steps, without minimizing hurt or skipping safety.Explore this approach →Somatic-informed therapyExplore how attention to sensation, movement, and the present environment can enter therapy. Understand the difference between somatic-informed care and a specific certified treatment.Explore this approach →Strengths-based therapyA strengths-based perspective considers abilities, relationships, and resources alongside needs. Explore how it differs from positive thinking, minimizing hardship, or making everything your responsibility.Explore this approach →Structural family therapyStructural family therapy examines roles, boundaries, and interaction patterns. Learn what joining, mapping, and enactments mean without assuming there is one correct family shape.Explore this approach →Trauma-informed therapyTrauma-informed describes how care is organized, not one trauma-treatment protocol. Learn what it can look like in practice, how consent should work, and how it differs from processing traumatic memories.Explore this approach →
